title: Robert Aumann of Jerusalem analyzed conflict and cooperation through game theory, and won the Nobel Prize in Economics

trailer.text: Robert Aumann is a professor emeritus in the Institute of Mathematics at the Hebrew University and a member of the interdisciplinary Center for the Study of Rationality.
He was born in 1930 in Frankfurt to an orthodox Jewish family, and he holds Israeli and US citizenship.
In 1938 his family emigrated to New York due to the Nazi persecution of Jews, and in 1956 he moved to Israel and began teaching mathematics at the Hebrew University.
According to the Swedish Academy, he was the first to conduct a full-fledged formal analysis of infinitely repeated games, and identified what outcomes can be upheld in long-run relations.
On October 10, 2005, he was named, together with Thomas Schelling, winner of the Nobel Prize in Economics, for having enhanced the understanding of conflict and cooperation through game theory.

stations.title: A home in Frankfurt and escape to New York

paragraphs.text: Aumann was born in 1930 in Frankfurt, Germany, to an orthodox Jewish family.
According to him, his father was a wholesale textile merchant who was financially comfortable, and his father's family had lived in Germany for centuries.
He said that the Nazi regime in the thirties made life very difficult for Jews in Germany.
In 1938 the family emigrated to New York due to the Nazi persecution of Jews.
According to the Forward, he was 8 at the time.
According to him, on the way his parents lost all their assets and had to work hard to make a living.

stations.title: Mathematics, then a problem about aircraft

paragraphs.text: Aumann said that he and his brother attended Jewish schools.
According to him, in high school he had an extraordinary teacher of mathematics, Abraham Gansler, who taught him to love the subject.
According to the Hebrew University, he received a bachelor's degree from City College of New York in 1950.
At MIT he decided to do a Ph.D. with Whitehead in knot theory, a branch of algebraic topology.
According to him, the thesis was published in the Annals of Mathematics in 1956.
After his doctorate, he said, he worked at an operations research consulting firm associated with Princeton University.
There he was assigned a problem: how to defend a city against a squadron of aircraft, a few of which carry nuclear weapons and most of which are decoys.
He remembered conversations with John Nash, and figured that game theory was the right tool for the problem.
Aumann said that when the State of Israel was established in 1948, he and his brother decided to make their lives there.
In 1956 he immigrated to Israel.
In the fall of 1956 he began working as an instructor of mathematics at the Hebrew University, and according to him he has been there ever since.
According to the Hebrew University, he became a full professor in 1968 and professor emeritus in 2000.
According to the university, he previously held the S.A. Schonbrunn Chair of Mathematical Economics.
He is a member of the interdisciplinary Center for the Study of Rationality.
According to the Swedish Academy, the question behind the work was why some groups, organizations and countries succeed in promoting cooperation while others suffer from conflict.
According to the Academy, in many situations cooperation may be easier to sustain in long-term relationships than in a single encounter.
According to the Academy, Aumann was the first to conduct a full-fledged formal analysis of infinitely repeated games.
According to the Academy, his research identified exactly what outcomes can be upheld over time in long-run relations.
According to MIT, he showed that cooperation increases when strategic situations are repeated.

The Academy added that cooperation is more difficult when there are many participants, when interactions are infrequent, when the relationship is likely to be broken off, or when the time horizon is short.
According to the Academy, these insights help explain price wars and trade wars, and why some communities manage common resources more successfully.
According to the Academy, they also clarify the reason for the existence of many institutions, from merchant guilds and organized crime to wage negotiations and international trade agreements.
Aumann said that the work the Committee mentioned most prominently when the Prize was announced was his 1959 paper, Acceptable Points in General Cooperative n-Person Games.
According to him, the paper shows that the strong equilibrium payoffs of a repeated game coincide with the core of the one-shot game.
According to MIT, one of his major contributions is correlated equilibrium, a concept that broadens the Nash equilibrium.
According to the Forward, he developed tools for analyzing economic systems in which player groups have great influence over the final result.
According to him, his work on repeated games with incomplete information began in the mid-sixties, in a project of the United States Arms Control and Disarmament Agency.
According to him, the aim was to help shape policy in the arms control talks with the Soviet Union.
He said that in 1995 the original reports were published as a book by MIT Press, and the book was awarded the Lanchester Prize for the best operations research book in 1995.
According to him, a question that Michael Maschler asked him after a lecture at the Hebrew University led to a lifelong scientific partnership.
According to him, this question led to their 1964 joint paper on the bargaining set for coalitional games.
He said that in a joint 1985 paper the two explained a difficult passage in the Babylonian Talmud, Ketubot, folio ninety-three, side a, by means of Schmeidler’s nucleolus.
According to him, in 1974 he wrote the book Values of Non-Atomic Games with Lloyd Shapley.
On October 10, 2005, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced the Bank of Sweden Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel for 2005.
The prize was awarded jointly to Aumann, of the Center for Rationality at the Hebrew University, and to Thomas Schelling.
The citation: they enhanced the understanding of conflict and cooperation through game-theory analysis.
The prize amount, SEK 10 million, was shared equally between the two.
According to MIT, the prize is worth $1.3 million.
According to Globes, the prize was to be awarded on December 10, which the newspaper describes as Alfred Nobel's birthday.
On October 10, 2005, the day of the announcement, the Hebrew University announced the win.
According to the university, he is the first currently affiliated faculty member of the university to receive a Nobel Prize.
The university's president, Prof. Menachem Magidor, said that the announcement brought pride and happiness to the university, to the State of Israel and to all of Israeli academia.
According to Globes, Aumann is the second Israeli to win the Nobel Prize for Economics, after Daniel Kahneman.
Kahneman, formerly a faculty member of the Hebrew University, won the prize in 2002.
According to MIT, Aumann is the third MIT-affiliated Nobel laureate in the field of game theory.
At the press conference, Aumann said that the prize is a prize for the world game theory community.

In the autobiography he wrote for the Nobel Foundation after the prize ceremony, he recounted seeing the flag of Israel fluttering next to the flag of Sweden on the roof of the Grand Hotel in Stockholm.
He described the win as a fairy-tale experience, but one that is not conducive to research, writing, teaching or any ordinary academic work, and stressed that this is not a complaint.
According to the Hebrew University, he has won the Israel Prize and many other honors.
According to MIT, he is a member of the national academies of sciences of the US and of Israel, the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and the British Academy.
According to MIT, he holds honorary doctorates from the Universities of Bonn, Louvain and Chicago.
Aumann said that his oldest son, Shlomo, was killed in action in 1982, while serving in the Israeli Army in the Lebanon War.
According to the Hebrew University, he is the father of five.
According to the Forward, colleagues said that he is a tolerant person and always ready to listen to other opinions.
According to the Forward, Aumann said that he has an explanation from game theory for the failure of the Oslo agreements.
According to the Forward, he said that the same tools help him explain why Israel must continue the arms race and hold on to nuclear weapons.
According to the Forward, he is a veteran member of the right-wing think tank "Professors for a Strong Israel" and opposed the disengagement from Gaza.
About the disengagement he said, irrespective of game theory, that in his view it was immoral, inhuman and stupid.
About his work on arms control, Aumann said that he doubts it had much practical influence on policy, though one can never know.

claims.text: לפי גלובס, אומן הוא הישראלי השני שזוכה בפרס נובל לכלכלה, אחרי דניאל כהנמן.
claims.quote: Aumann, a professor emeritus in the Hebrew University Institute of Mathematics, is the second Israeli to win the Nobel Prize for Economics.

claims.text: דניאל כהנמן, לשעבר חבר סגל באוניברסיטה העברית ובהמשך בפרינסטון, זכה בפרס נובל לכלכלה ב-2002.
claims.quote: Prof. Daniel Kahneman, formerly a faculty member of the Hebrew University and now at Princeton University, also won the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2002

claims.text: אומן אמר במסיבת העיתונאים שהפרס הוא פרס לקהילת תורת המשחקים העולמית.
claims.quote: This is a prize for the world game theory community

claims.text: אומן סיפר שראה את דגל ישראל מתנופף ליד דגל שוודיה על גג הגראנד הוטל בשטוקהולם.
claims.quote: Seeing the flag of Israel fluttering in the wind, right next to that of Sweden, from the roof of the Grand Hotel in Stockholm.

claims.text: אומן תיאר את הזכייה בפרס נובל כחוויה אגדית, אך כזו שאינה מאפשרת מחקר, כתיבה או הוראה רגילים.
claims.quote: Being awarded the Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel is a beautiful, fairy-tale experience, from beginning to end.

claims.text: לפי MIT, אומן חבר באקדמיות הלאומיות למדעים של ארה"ב ושל ישראל, באקדמיה האמריקאית לאמנויות ולמדעים ובאקדמיה הבריטית.
claims.quote: Aumann is a member of the (U.S.) National Academy of Sciences, the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, the Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the British Academy.

claims.text: לפי MIT, אומן מחזיק בתארי דוקטור כבוד מאוניברסיטאות בון, לובן ושיקגו.
claims.quote: He holds honorary doctorates from the Universities of Bonn, Louvain and Chicago.

claims.text: אומן סיפר שבנו הבכור שלמה נהרג בקרב ב-1982 בשירותו בצבא הישראלי במלחמת של"ג.
claims.quote: the oldest, Shlomo, was killed in action in 1982, while serving in the Israeli Army in

claims.text: לפי האוניברסיטה העברית, אומן אב לחמישה וסב ל-18.
claims.quote: He is the father of five and the grandfather of 18.

claims.text: לפי ה-Forward, עמיתים אמרו על אומן שהוא אדם סובלני ותמיד מוכן להקשיב לדעות אחרות.
claims.quote: is a tolerant person and is always ready to listen to other opinions

claims.text: לפי ה-Forward, אומן אמר שיש לו הסבר מתורת המשחקים לכישלון הסכמי אוסלו.
claims.quote: Aumann said that he has an explanation from game theory for the failure of the Oslo agreements

claims.text: לפי ה-Forward, אומן אמר שאותם כלים מסייעים לו להסביר מדוע ישראל חייבת להמשיך במרוץ החימוש ולהחזיק בנשק גרעיני.
claims.quote: the same tools help him explain why Israel must continue the arms race and hold on to nuclear weapons.

claims.text: לפי ה-Forward, אומן חבר ותיק בצוות החשיבה הימני "פרופסורים למען ישראל חזקה" והתנגד להתנתקות מעזה.
claims.quote: Aumann is a veteran member of right-wing think tank Professors for a Strong Israel, and he opposed the Gaza pullout.

claims.text: אומן אמר על ההתנתקות מעזה, במובחן מתורת המשחקים, שלדעתו הייתה בלתי מוסרית, בלתי אנושית וטיפשית.
claims.quote: Irrespective of game theory, I think it was immoral, inhuman, and stupid

claims.text: אומן סיפר שהוא מפקפק אם לעבודה זו הייתה השפעה מעשית רבה על המדיניות, אם כי אי אפשר לדעת.
claims.quote: I doubt that this work did indeed have much practical influence on policy, though one can never know

claims.text: לפי האוניברסיטה העברית, אומן כתב כמעט 100 מאמרים מדעיים ושישה ספרים.
claims.quote: He is the author nearly 100 scientific papers and six books.

claims.text: לפי MIT, אומן פרסם חמישה ספרים ויותר מ-70 מאמרים מדעיים.
claims.quote: Aumann has published five books and more than 70 scientific papers.

claims.text: לפי MIT, התעניינותו של אומן בתורת המשחקים החלה ב-1956, עם הצטרפותו למכון למתמטיקה באוניברסיטה העברית.
claims.quote: His interest turned to game theory in 1956, when he joined the Mathematics Institute at Jerusalem's Hebrew University, where he has been ever since.

claims.text: בסתיו 1956 החל לעבוד כמדריך למתמטיקה באוניברסיטה העברית, ולדבריו הוא נמצא שם מאז.
claims.quote: In the fall of 1956 I took up a position as instructor of mathematics at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem
claims.checker_note: audit: quote found on the fetched page

claims.text: באוטוביוגרפיה שכתב לקרן נובל אחרי טקס הפרס סיפר שראה את דגל ישראל מתנופף ליד דגל שוודיה על גג הגראנד הוטל בשטוקהולם.
claims.quote: Seeing the flag of Israel fluttering in the wind, right next to that of Sweden, from the roof of the Grand Hotel in Stockholm.
claims.checker_note: audit: quote found on the fetched page

claims.text: לדבריו, אביו היה סוחר טקסטיל סיטונאי במצב כלכלי נוח, ומשפחת אביו חיה בגרמניה מאות שנים.
claims.quote: My father was a wholesale textile merchant, financially comfortable, whose family had lived in Germany for centuries
claims.checker_note: audit: quote found on the fetched page

claims.text: לדבריו, עם לויד שפלי כתב ב-1974 את הספר Values of Non-Atomic Games.
claims.quote: Prominent among them is Lloyd Shapley, with whom I coauthored the 1974 book Values of Non-Atomic Games
